merger_description:
AAH Veterinary Services Pty Ltd (**AAH**), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Apiam Animal Health Limited (**Apiam**), proposes to acquire 100% of the business and business assets of Goulburn Valley Equine Hospital (the **Acquisition**).

Apiam is a rural veterinary business, comprising more than 80 veterinary clinics and ancillary business sites across Australia, and supplies a range of veterinary services across Australia. This includes companion animal, equine, dairy, beef cattle, sheep and goat, pig, poultry and mixed animal veterinary services, together with veterinary diagnostics, emergency and after-hours services, reproductive and herd health services, and pathology, laboratory and advisory services. Apiam is ultimately owned and controlled by funds managed and advised by Adamantem Capital Management.

Goulburn Valley Equine Hospital is located in the Goulburn Valley region in Shepparton, Victoria. It primarily supplies complete equine veterinary services, including ambulatory services and specialist equine referral services in the fields of lameness, medicine, surgery, dental and reproduction.

events.title: Apiam - Goulburn Valley Equine Hospital - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
The ACCC found that the Parties do not compete closely in the
supply of certain equine veterinary services, including emergency
and ambulatory services and general equine veterinary care, due to
the distance of the Apiam equine veterinary locations from Goulburn
Valley Equine Hospital and the limited overlap in the geographic
areas serviced by the facilities. The merged entity would, in any
event, continue to face competition from alternative providers of
these equine veterinary services.
The Parties also overlap in the supply of equine referral hospital
services, including complex surgeries as well as advanced
reproductive services (such as artificial insemination and embryo
transfer). In relation to these services, the ACCC found that
customers are willing to travel significant distances in order to
access treatment for their horses. As such, the ACCC considers that
post-Acquisition, Apiam would continue to face competition from
alternative equine hospitals and clinics providing these services,
located across a broad geographic area.
The ACCC notes that some third parties raised concerns about the
potential for increased prices and/or decreased service quality as a
result of corporate ownership of Goulburn Valley Equine Hospital.
However, these concerns did not relate to the likely competitive
effects of the Acquisition.
